decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5 to 5-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Economic activity expanded at a modest pace in the first quarter.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this language to note that economic activity grew at a modest pace in the first quarter of the year.

changes.quote: Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: The language was streamlined to confirm that job gains remain robust and unemployment is still low.

changes.quote: Tighter credit conditions for households and businesses are likely to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation.
changes.explanation: The Fed removed the reference to recent banking developments, directly noting that tighter credit conditions are expected to weigh on the economy.

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 5 to 5-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: This updates the target range to reflect the new 25 basis point rate increase.

changes.quote: In determining the extent to which additional policy firming may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy...
changes.explanation: The phrase changed from future increases to additional policy firming, signaling a potential shift in how future rate decisions are evaluated.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 19.07% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.38% and moved -6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.39% would fall by about $11.76 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.5%, and employers added an average of 264k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4.9% over the past year (March 2023); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 4.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -8 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -0.7%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.41% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future policy decisions will depend on cumulative tightening and economic data rather than a preset path. An educational forecast model suggests the next meeting has a 27% chance of a hold, a 1% chance of a cut, and a 72% chance of a hike.
